examples.problem:
Compute $P\left( 1 \lt   X \lt 3 \right)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040290/assets/394c60a510e39043cda5072c0b57a663b200275035d72c15f20c5a257e6c4fc0.png)
examples.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a \lt   X \lt      b) = \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<X<3) & ={\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{18}({x}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{18}{\int }_{1}^{3}({x}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{18}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-x]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}([\frac{1}{3}(3)^{3}-(3)]-[\frac{1}{3}(1)^{3}-(1)]) \\  & =\frac{1}{18}([9-3]-[\frac{1}{3}-1]) \\  & =\frac{1}{18}(6+\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{18}\cdot \frac{20}{3} \\  & =\frac{10}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$
